newsitem.title: BULGARIA: New Bulgarian president sworn in, calls for polls.
newsitem.headline: New Bulgarian president sworn in, calls for polls.

text.p: Bulgaria's new president Petar Stoyanov was sworn in on Sunday and said elections must be held as soon as possible.
"Bulgaria wants elections as soon as possible, Bulgaria must get these elections," he told parliament.

Parliament's Socialist majority has offered elections by the end of the year but the opposition wants them sooner and has organised 13 consecutive days of mass protests against economic hardship and the Socialist government.
Stoyanov and his vice-president, Todor Kavaldzhiev, were sworn in by parliamentary speaker Blagovest Sendov.
"Today I address you convinced that the country needs early elections and a new social contract," Stoyanov said.
"Elections which bring more consensus into society, elections which will let the new rulers together with the people flooding the streets carry out the painful but vital economic reforms."
